item.title: LeBron James Is on “a Hell of a Ride.” Now He’s Got a New Maybach for the Journey.
item.description: The NBA’s all-time leading scorer has owned vehicles from Lamborghini, Ferrari, and Rolls-Royce. Now he unveils the latest addition to his collection: a one-off Mercedes-Maybach S 680.

item.title: The AI Economy Is “Propped Up by a Ponzi Scheme,” Says Director of ‘The AI Doc’
item.description: Daniel Roher calls himself an “apocaloptimist,” meaning he’s supposedly bullish about the AI revolution. But in conversation, those positive vibes aren’t always easy to come by.

item.title: The Story of Charvet (Or, How to Keep Luxury Quiet)
item.description: The French shirtmaker Charvet is more talked about than ever—and the family behind it wishes we’d be more discreet. Marisa Meltzer visits with Jean-Claude and Anne-Marie Colban, the siblings who run the business and dress its discerning clientele.

item.title: Valerie Cherish Answers the Proust Questionnaire
item.description: The sitcom star, HBO ‘Comeback’ queen, and, okay, fictional character—created by Lisa Kudrow and Michael Patrick King—waxes poetic about honesty, dishonesty, and Marky Mark. (No, not that one.)

item.title: Miley Cyrus on Finding Sobriety After Being a Child Star: “My Life Is So Beautiful”
item.description: On the 20th anniversary of ‘Hannah Montana,’ Cyrus talks her career, family relationships, and road to recovery.

item.title: Supergirl Milly Alcock Prepares to Take Flight
item.description: She rode dragons in Westeros and scammed Julianne Moore on Sirens. Now the Aussie is taking on a beloved comic book character: “I am aware that I am going to get comments,” she says. “But I can’t really stop them. I can only be myself.”

item.title: Kate Middleton’s Former Stylist Starts Her Own Agency
item.description: What can we expect from the new consulting firm of Natasha Archer, who spent 15 years styling the Princess of Wales?

item.title: How Locals Really Feel About The White Lotus Coming to Town in St. Tropez
item.description: After successful outings in the likes of Sicily and Thailand, the smash-hit series is headed for France's glitziest coastline—but how do locals feel about such a strong spotlight?

item.title: Love March Madness? Thank the Man Who Made It Easier to Watch
item.description: More than fifteen years ago, TV exec David Levy had a bright idea: What if every NCAA tournament game could be available all at once? As he says in a new interview, it would prove to be “life changing for everybody.”

item.title: An Amateur Investigation Into The Magnani-Rocca Foundation Heist
item.description: Earlier this month, three paintings—a Renoir, a Matisse, and a Cézanne—were stolen in minutes, and the news didn’t break for almost a week. Vanity Fair Italy took a trip to Villa Magnani in Traversetolo for reconnaissance.

item.title: Exclusive: OpenAI Preps Policy Push to “Rethink the Social Contract”
item.description: Is OpenAI’s chief futurist prepping for a major breakthrough or just another hype cycle?

item.title: 23 Books in 23 Days: Everything Jeremy O. Harris Read While Imprisoned in Japan
item.description: In the quiet of my cell, I realized how loud my normal life had become.

item.title: Jeremy O. Harris Recounts His 23 Days Imprisoned In Japan
item.description: In America, a lawyer can swoop in, call in a favor with the DA she went to law school with and you’re saved. A wealthy parent or a friend can post bail. In Japan, a gaijin (foreigner) is on their own.

item.title: What Happened on Euphoria Season 2—and What We’d Like to See in Season 3
item.description: Four years after its season 2 finale, Euphoria is finally back on HBO—reuniting Zendaya, Jacob Elordi, Sydney Sweeney, and the rest of the crew. Can’t remember where we left their characters? VF is here to help.
